Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 32 (Switch missing-address campaign): added the Citadel Campus shared address and full-build-out context from the operators own press release. research_status remains complete.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility, Tahoe Reno 5, is part of Switchs Citadel Campus (Tahoe Reno) in Storey County, Nevada. Per Switchs own press release announcing the Tahoe Reno campus opening (tier-1 operator source, https://www.switch.com/switch-tahoe-reno-data-center-now-open/), this is the Citadel Campus, a 2,000 acre site in the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center in Storey County, Nevada, next to the Tesla Gigafactory, designed for up to 7.2 million square feet and up to 650 MW of power at full build out, a small fraction of which this registry currently tracks as five buildings. Aggregator directories (datacenterHawk, DataCenterMap) give 1 Superloop Circle, Reno, NV as the address for this campus, the same address appears attached to more than one individually numbered Tahoe Reno building on these directories, so it is treated here as a shared campus level address rather than a distinct address for any one building. Switch own official locations page (fetched directly this session, https://www.switch.com/locations/) names five exascale campuses, the Citadel in Tahoe Reno, the Pyramid Campus in Grand Rapids, the Core Campus in Las Vegas, the Keep Campus in Atlanta, and the Rock Campus in Austin and Houston, but confirms no street address for any campus or building, directing visitors to a contact form instead. This registry rows address, where given below, therefore comes from data center industry aggregator directories, leads-only sources per this projects source hierarchy, not confirmed directly by the operator.

reading.body:
Tahoe Reno 5 is one building in Switch's Citadel Campus, a 2,000-acre site in Storey County designed for up to 650 MW across 7.2 million square feet at full buildout. The facility specifications provided do not include a published power or IT load figure for this building alone, only the campus-level target. Without a megawatt specification for Tahoe Reno 5 itself, its capacity relative to the AI infrastructure this site tracks cannot be stated.

Nevada has 26 mapped data center facilities, of which only two publish power capacity figures, totaling 10.37 MW. Tahoe Reno 5 is ranked third by published capacity in the state, though this ranking reflects the absence of published figures from other sites rather than confirmed capacity data for this campus. The state context does not include a published megawatt figure that would place this facility in the ranking.

The Citadel Campus full buildout of 650 MW across multiple buildings would position it as significant infrastructure were it completed, but Switch has not published per-building capacity for Tahoe Reno 5 on its specification pages this site has read. Until the operator publishes a megawatt figure for this specific facility or building, its role in Nevada's AI power footprint remains unquantified in this registry.
